title: An LLM-Orchestrated Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Verifying Diagnostic Signal Reachability in Electronic Systems
title_zh: 一种用于验证电子系统诊断信号可达性的大模型编排神经符号框架

paragraphs.en: 提出NetFlow-DSR神经符号框架，用LLM结合图引擎自动验证诊断信号可达性。 Diagnostic Signal Reachability (DSR) captures whether board-level health signals are observable by management controllers, including baseboard management controllers (BMCs), complex programmable logic devices (CPLDs), and other smart controllers. Verifying DSR is essential for field diagnosability in datacenter fleets, where one design is deployed at massive scale, yet it remains largely manual, since each signal is traced by hand across schematic sheets, renamed nets, series components, and monitoring devices. Large language models (LLMs) are attractive but unreliable at structural connectivity reasoning, where over-claiming can silently hide a rare coverage gap. We present NetFlow-DSR, a neuro-symbolic framework in which an LLM orchestrates the DSR pipeline and resolves device roles mainly from part-name families and library pin names, consulting specifications only for ambiguous parts. Pin directionality is read from the design library, and deterministic graph engines verify connectivity over the authoritative netlist. The pipeline detects diagnostic nets, canonicalizes renamed net fragments, and performs controller-seeded, power-aware breadth-first search over an admissibility graph that credits device-mediated monitoring. Each verdict carries an auditable trace card whose proof path is the witness. Across five production boards from an AI platform, covering 421 expert-graded signals, a three-stage ablation improves pooled F1 from 0.578 to 0.944. Because a monitored verdict is emitted only with a proof path, the verifier is sound by construction, and precision and specificity were 100% in the evaluated data. In a cross-model study on the system-controller module, precision remained 100% across three LLMs while recall tracked each model's device-semantic extraction. Precision therefore depends on the netlist-grounded verifier and correct device semantics rather than on any single LLM.
paragraphs.zh: 提出NetFlow-DSR神经符号框架，用LLM结合图引擎自动验证诊断信号可达性。诊断信号可达性（DSR）刻画板级健康信号是否能被管理控制器观测到，包括基板管理控制器（BMC）、复杂可编程逻辑器件（CPLD）及其他智能控制器。 验证DSR对于数据中心大规模部署单一设计机群在现场的可诊断性至关重要，但目前仍主要依赖人工，因为每个信号都需要手工跨原理图页面、重命名的网络、串联元件和监控设备进行追踪。 大语言模型（LLM）颇具吸引力，但在结构连接性推理上并不可靠，过度断言可能会悄然掩盖罕见的覆盖缺口。 我们提出NetFlow-DSR，这是一个神经符号框架，其中LLM负责编排DSR流程，并主要依据器件名称家族和库引脚名称来判定器件角色，仅在器件存在歧义时查阅规格书。 引脚方向性从设计库中读取，确定性图引擎在权威网表上验证连接性。 该流程检测诊断网络，规范化重命名的网络片段，并在一个认可器件介导监控的可达性图上执行以控制器为起点、感知电源的广度优先搜索。 每个判定都附带可审计的追踪卡，其证明路径即为证据。 在来自某AI平台的五块生产板上，覆盖421个专家评级信号，三阶段消融实验将合并F1从0.578提升至0.944。 由于只有在存在证明路径时才输出「已监控」判定，验证器在构造上是可靠的，且在评估数据中精确率和特异度均为100%。 在针对系统控制器模块的跨模型研究中，三种LLM的精确率均保持100%，而召回率则随各模型的器件语义抽取能力而变化。 因此，精确率取决于基于网表的验证器和正确的器件语义，而非任何单一的LLM。
